analysis:
Examined the supplied changes. Darkbloom.swift (head line 32) registers a new `Addon.self` subcommand. StatusCommand+AddonHold.swift (lines 4-12) adds a read-only status line, and StatusCommand.swift (head line 118) prints it from DaemonState.addonHold. The new AddonCommandTests file covers parsing (lease bounds 30-600s), liveIdentity freshness and process-identity checks, and the DaemonState JSON round-trip of the hold snapshot.

The status line only formats local daemon-state data, so it adds no network, crypto, or authorization surface. Addon.describe, Addon.liveIdentity, Addon.Hold, Addon.Release and the daemon-side add-on hold mechanism are not in the supplied evidence. Their implementation is in other batches or outside this one, so this pass cannot judge the security of the IPC/control channel behind `addon hold` and `addon release --force`.

Questions for integration. (1) How does the hold command authenticate to the provider? The tests suggest it targets a ProcessIdentity read from the daemon state file, which is a local file an unprivileged local process could in principle influence. (2) Can a local actor with state-file access cause a persistent denial of service by holding the provider, i.e. T-043/TB-003-style availability? Lease bounds appear to be enforced at the CLI only, and the daemon-side cap is unverified. (3) Does the hold interact with the add-on VM machine lock without weakening TB-003 or TB-007? (4) Does any addon-hold state reach the coordinator, and does it affect A-016 serving authorization? None of this is observable here.

No concrete regression is identifiable in the supplied lines, so there are no findings. The unverified daemon-side hold/IPC contract warrants a deeper look wherever the Addon implementation appears.
